newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X say Busang may be open to negotiation.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X say Busang may be open to negotiation.

text.p: Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd said on Thursday that the huge Busang gold find in Indonesia is "possibly open to negotiation" and that draft documents show it has exclusive operating rights to Busang.
Bre-X also said in a statement that it is seeking to clarify comments made earlier by Indonesian Mines and Energy Ministry secretary-general Umar Said.
Said told Reuters Thursday that Bre-X and Barrick Gold Corp must seek fresh contracts of work to develop the gold find, estimated by Bre-X to contain at least 57 million ounces of gold.

The Indonesian government, in a letter last month, told Bre-X and Barrick to enter a partnership agreement, with Bre-X retaining a 25 percent stake in the find and Barrick 75 percent. The two companies have not yet struck a deal.

Commenting on news reports that Indonesian President Suharto has become involved in the matter, Bre-X chairman David Walsh said it "indicates that the process of determining the best way to develop this extraordinary natural resource is possibly open to negotiation." Bre-X also attempted to clarify its rights to the Busang find under draft agreements signed earlier with the Indonesian government.

Trading in Bre-X's stock was halted on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Wednesday so company officials could respond to comments from Indonesia's Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana. Sudjana said Wednesday that the government had cancelled parliamentary approval of applications for contracts of work made by Bre-X to develop the richest parts of Busang.

Bre-X has a contract of work for the Busang I area of the property which contains only an estimated 2.6 million ounces of gold. The bulk of the precious metal is in two adjoining lots, Busang II and Busang III, for which it needs contracts of work to explore and develop.

"Article 2 of the draft CoW (contract of work) initialed by Parliament clearly states that Bre-X has an exclusive right pertaining to surveying, mining, processing and marketing of products from the contract area," Bre-X said in a letter sent to Sudjana on Thursday.

Bre-X said the appropriate and customary process for including a new partner in Busang is by way of article 29, or the so-called "assignment clause" of the draft contract of work wherein the government can approve or reject a proposed partner. "This process can only take place after the CoW has been signed," Bre-X said in the letter.

Bre-X said it believes that development of the Busang deposit should begin as quickly as possible. In this regard, the company said a final feasibility study report on Busang 1 will be submitted by mid-December to Indonesia's Directorate General of Mining.
"Upon receipt of government approval by Bre-X in accordance with CoW requirements, the company will be in a position to expedite construction and development," the company said in the letter.
